what_this_is: Relations BETWEEN families. Every relation transfers zero occurrences. This is the file that keeps a limb family from lending its sitting count to the whole question it sits inside.

horizon.rationale: Founder decision. 2010 is the permanent lower boundary of MIW Question Intelligence and 2026-08 the ceiling of this Phase-1 release. Pre-2010 material already held in the repository is ARCHIVE CONTEXT ONLY and may never enter governed recurrence. No pre-2010 acquisition backlog exists or may be created.

verdict_vocabulary.SAME_FAMILY: Same examinable answer core, same ask. One family.
verdict_vocabulary.SAME_FAMILY_VARIANT: Same answer core; wording, limb count or framing differs. One family, variant recorded.
verdict_vocabulary.SAME_LIMB_FAMILY: Two limbs that ask the same thing across sittings. One limb family.
verdict_vocabulary.WHOLE_VS_LIMB_RELATION: One is a limb of the other. TWO families, related, sharing no occurrence.
verdict_vocabulary.RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT: Same topic, different examinable answer core. Two families, related.
verdict_vocabulary.DISTINCT: Not the same question. No relation recorded.
verdict_vocabulary.CURRENT_FRAMEWORK_CHANGED: Same ask, but the governing framework moved so far that the answer core is no longer the same.
verdict_vocabulary.AMBIGUOUS_HOLD: Cannot be settled on held evidence. No join is made and the pair stays visible.

limb_rule: A limb occurrence may never be counted as a whole-question occurrence, and a whole-question occurrence may never be counted as a limb occurrence. Two families related by WHOLE_VS_LIMB_RELATION share no occurrence.

joins.reason: The exhaust-emission short-notes bundle is set in a four-limb form (Tier II/III regulation, primary vs secondary NOx, SCR, scavenge-air moisturising and EGR) and a two-limb form (primary vs secondary NOx, SAM and EGR). The two-limb form requires neither the Tier II/III regulatory limits nor SCR, which is half the preparation. Two families, related.

QIE-H-59566 asks ONLY the charter-survey comparison -- limbs (c) and (d) of the four-limb bill-of-lading question. It holds eight governed occurrences of its own. Merged, those eight sittings would be read as eight sittings of the whole bill-of-lading question, which has been set far less often. This is the exact inflation the limb model exists to prevent.
Asymmetric containment: one stem is largely contained in the other while the reverse is not. Recorded as a relation so the smaller unit can never lend its sitting count to the larger.
